title: Philadelphia Fed First Quarter 2027 Survey of Professional Forecasters — 10:00 a.m. ET, dated by construction rule alone and filed as that rule's own out-of-sample test
source: EST: DERIVED, not read — and that is stated plainly because no primary source for this date exists yet. The Philadelphia Fed's calendar endpoint (philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200, 131,096 bytes) carries 237 rows and every one of them is dated 2026; the bank has not published a 2027 schedule. The date here is computed from the construction rule the survey-of-professional-forecasters-q4-2026-11-16 initial research derived from the publisher's own 'Dates of Previous Surveys' file (spf-release-dates.txt, HTTP 200, 8,298 bytes, 146 quarters since 1990Q2): the response deadline is the Tuesday of the second week of the quarter's middle month, and the news release follows exactly 3 business days later once weekends and the Veterans Day federal holiday are excluded — 40 of 59 quarters since 2012 at exactly 3 business days, 53 of 59 at 3 or 4, with both larger outliers being the government-shutdown quarters the file itself footnotes. The second Tuesday of February 2027 is Tue 2027-02-09; three business days later, with no federal holiday intervening (Presidents Day 2027 falls on Mon 2027-02-15, after the release), is Fri 2027-02-12. Two independent checks agree: Q1 releases have landed on a Friday 15 times out of 15 since 2012, and every Q1 release since 2005 has fallen between the 9th and the 15th of February except the two shutdown-delayed ones. Filed estimate on the strongest possible grounds for that label — the date is an inference from a cadence record, no page anywhere states it, and this lane never self-confirms. Derived 2026-09-09 during the never-assessed initial research of survey-of-professional-forecasters-q4-2026-11-16
notes: PROPOSED (not canonical) by the survey-of-professional-forecasters-q4-2026-11-16 initial-research adjacency sweep on 2026-09-09. THIS PROPOSAL IS DELIBERATELY WEAKER THAN A NORMAL ONE AND EXISTS TO BE FALSIFIED. Every other proposal on this shelf carries a date somebody published; this one carries a date this repo computed, and it is filed precisely so the Philadelphia Fed's eventual 2027 calendar adjudicates the construction rule the proposer's ledger derived, rather than that rule sitting unfalsified in a document. If the bank publishes 2027-02-12 at 10:00 a.m., the rule survives its first out-of-sample test and every future SPF instance becomes datable in advance. If it publishes any other date, the rule is wrong, this file is deleted, and the proposer's ledger — which registers the identical rule as forward test FT-survey-of-professional-forecasters-q4-2026-11-16-1 against the 2026-11-16 print — has its central derivation weakened on the record. Either outcome is a result. WHY THE INSTRUMENT IS WORTH A ROW AT ALL, at LOW: the SPF is the oldest quarterly macro-forecast survey in the United States, running since 1968, taken over by the Philadelphia Fed in 1990, and the source FOMC-watchers quote for consensus CPI, core PCE, GDP and unemployment paths. But the proposer's ledger measured what it does to a tape and the answer is nothing — absolute close-to-close moves on 95 SPF release days 2003-2026 are statistically indistinguishable from all other days across the 10-year breakeven (ratio 0.97, Welch t=-0.34), the 5-year breakeven, VIX and the 10-year note. Impact LOW and symbols [] are therefore inherited from a measurement, not from a convention. Whoever writes the canonical file owns (a) replacing this derived date with the bank's published 2027 row the moment one exists, (b) recording whether the rule held, and (c) scoring FT-survey-of-professional-forecasters-q4-2026-11-16-1 if the Q4 2026 print has not already settled it. A DECLINE with reasoning recorded is an acceptable outcome and, for a date nobody has published, an especially defensible one. This is a PROPOSAL and an ESTIMATE: it widens caution and licenses nothing.
